strategy.why_this_method: The expression is a product of x squared and a composite sine function, so each structure needs its own rule.
strategy.alternatives: Expanding is impossible because sine of 3x is not a polynomial. The product and chain rules are the direct method.

steps.title: Set up the product rule
steps.explanation: There are two factors, and both depend on x. Differentiate one factor at a time while leaving the other unchanged.
steps.common_mistake: Do not multiply the two derivatives; that is not the product rule.

steps.title: Differentiate the polynomial factor
steps.explanation: The exponent comes down as a coefficient and decreases by one. This supplies the derivative of the first factor.

steps.title: Differentiate the sine composition
steps.explanation: Differentiate the outer sine first, then multiply by the derivative of the inner function 3x. The inner derivative is the extra factor 3.
steps.common_mistake: Forgetting the factor 3 is the most common chain-rule error here.

steps.title: Combine the product-rule terms
steps.explanation: Substitute both derivatives into the product-rule setup. The two unlike terms cannot be combined further.

final_answer.plain: The derivative is 2x sin(3x) plus 3x squared cos(3x).
final_answer.domain_notes: The derivative exists for every real x.

check.method: evaluated a symmetric difference quotient numerically
check.detail: The symbolic derivative agrees with the numerical slope at test values.

hints: Notice both a product and a function inside another function.
Apply the product rule first, then the chain rule to sin(3x).
The derivative of sin(3x) is 3 cos(3x).
